title: Fast Ethernet
markdown:
## Fast Ethernet

Fast Ethernet was designed to compete with LAN protocols such as FDDI
or Fiber Channel. IEEE created Fast Ethernet under the name **802.3u**.
Fast Ethernet is backward-compatible with Standard Ethernet but
transmits data 10 times faster, at 100 Mbps.

### Fast Ethernet Topology

Two panels:
- **(a) Point-to-point**: two stations connected directly by a single
  line, no intermediate device.
- **(b) Star**: a **Switch** box at top connects down to three
  stations, each via its own line.

{{viz:0}}

### Fast Ethernet Implementations

| Characteristics | 100Base-TX | 100Base-FX | 100Base-T4 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Media | Cat 5 UTP or STP | Fiber | Cat 4 UTP |
| Number of wires | 2 | 2 | 4 |
| Maximum length | 100 m | 100 m | 100 m |
| Block encoding | 4B/5B | 4B/5B | *(none)* |
| Line encoding | MLT-3 | NRZ-I | 8B/6T |

{{viz:1}}

### Encoding for Fast Ethernet

Three station-block diagrams:

- **100Base-TX**: 4×25 Mbps lines feed a yellow **4B/5B encoder** block
  → 125 Mbps → a pink **MLT-3 encoder** block → out over **two UTP
  category 5** wires (and symmetric decoder path back: MLT-3 decoder →
  4B/5B decoder → 4×25 Mbps).
- **100Base-FX**: identical two-stage structure (yellow **4B/5B
  encoder** → pink **NRZ-I encoder**) but the outbound medium is
  **two fibers** instead of UTP.
- **100Base-T4**: a single-stage pink **8B/6T encoder**/**decoder** pair
  (100 Mbps in/out, no separate block-encoding stage), fanning out to
  **4 category 3 UTP** wires with a mix of send/receive/bidirectional
  arrows.

{{viz:2}}
